properties.name: Three finding kinds stop reading a brainstorm as a commitment
properties.rationale:
THE ROOT CAUSE IS THE HAND-MAINTENANCE, NOT THE THREE CALL SITES. The principle "a proposed Decision asserts nothing" was already written down in FOUR places and implemented in ONE: `zero_degree_finding` grades a proposed Decision to `info` as "a parked thought that correctly shapes nothing yet"; schema/inference.yaml says "ONLY AN ACCEPTED DECISION DISCONTINUES ANYTHING"; `loop_status` stays quiet on a proposed Decision with no approver; and the `parks` ruling requires an accepted Decision, which is why parks could not reach this case. Every detector nevertheless re-derived its qualifier set by hand, so `contradiction` grew `alignment=supporting` and then `rejected`/`superseded` one incident at a time while the other two grew nothing.

THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS, AND IT WAS PREDICTED IN ADVANCE. `chg:unallocated-component-reads-the-ruling` recorded hours before the field report arrived: "nothing checks that a NEW structural detector reads the ruling. The next one written will have the same hole for the same reason." F-01's replay contract, enforced field by field with nothing checking it, is the same shape. So the guard is the deliverable: `every_category_states_whether_it_reads_proposed` is an exhaustive match over `HealCategory`, and a new category cannot compile until its author has written down where it stands. Both answers are legitimate; an unconsidered category is not.

⭐ THE FIRST CUT WAS WRONG AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT IT. Folding `proposed` in with `rejected`/`superseded` broke `a_proposed_decision_is_not_treated_as_withdrawn`, a deliberate counterweight holding that "a parked idea that conflicts with an accepted decision is a real thing to settle". That test is right and was not overridden: a withdrawal is a positive act that RETIRES a conflict and skips on EITHER side, while being unclaimed skips only when NEITHER side claims anything. hxm_program's field case was proposed-vs-PROPOSED, which nothing covered; the counterweight's case is proposed-vs-ACCEPTED. Both shapes now have a test.

⚠️ A SECOND WRONG ASSUMPTION, ALSO PINNED. The change was first documented as inert on existing designs by analogy with "silence keeps its historical meaning". False: `Decision.status` carries `default: proposed`, so silence was never reachable and every proposed Decision in every design changes behaviour. `a_decision_has_no_unlabelled_state` exists to kill that assumption for the next reader. The scope counterweight is the node TYPE — `CONTRADICTS` is declared `from: "*" to: "*"` and `Requirement.status` also defaults to `proposed`, so an untyped predicate would have silenced conflicts between the 51 requirements merely awaiting the user's word.

FIRST WORKED EXAMPLE OF `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` DONE IN FULL: the pin was written first and OBSERVED FAILING (4 of 10, reproducing all three finding kinds, with the counterweights passing before the fix so they are not vacuous), then the fix, then green. F-01 could only claim the test passed after; this one saw it fail first.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `is_parked_idea` added to crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs — one predicate (a Decision at `status: proposed`), read by three finding kinds that previously read a brainstorm's edges as commitments. `contradiction` and `unresolved_setup` skip when BOTH endpoints are parked ideas; `unthreaded_cluster` skips an island where EVERY member is. `unresolved_setup` had no endpoint filter of any kind before this. `duplicate` and the three pure-topology rules deliberately do NOT read it. Measured on reflow2's own design: 89 -> 78 structural defects. New pin at crates/reflow2-core/tests/proposed_asserts_nothing.rs (10 tests); tests/contradiction_alignment.rs now states `accepted` on its two decisions instead of leaning silently on the schema default. Core suite 1500 passed / 0 failed across 130 binaries; fmt and clippy clean.
